passage:
A group of students started a fact-check corner in the school newspaper. Each week, they examined a popular claim heard online or around school.
They checked sources, dates, images, and expert explanations. Sometimes the claim was false. Sometimes it was partly true but missing context.
At first, some classmates disliked being corrected. The team learned to write politely and explain their method.
The fact-check corner became one of the most-read sections.
The team learned that truth is not protected by confidence. It is protected by careful work. Correcting information is not about looking smarter. It is about keeping a community from being misled.
